title: Your Lead Problem Is Not a Lead Problem
descriptions:
Everyone's obsessed with leads.

That's the wrong obsession.


We've built entire organizations around one question: "How many leads did we get today?"

CRMs full of data.

Portals burning cash.

Teams on standby.

Conversion rates that haven't moved in years.

The lead was never the problem.

The system after the lead was.


What actually moves inventory:

→ Training - your team closes deals, not your portal

→ Experience - every touchpoint is a sales moment

→ Automation - follow-ups that don't depend on someone's mood

→ Feedback loops - know why every deal died

→ Monitoring - real-time pipeline, not end-of-month surprises

→ Old lead revival - your best leads are already in your database

→ Referral activation - one happy buyer = three warm introductions

→ Self-generated leads - a brand that pulls, not just paid that pushes

→ Organic marketing - content that pre-sells before the first call

→ Past client reactivation - they trust you. You forgot to call.


Real estate is not a lead problem.

It's a conversion infrastructure problem.

The industry has gigabytes of data and kilobytes of strategy.


We measure cost-per-lead.

We should be measuring revenue-per-system.

Real estate is simple.

How fast can you sell?

Not how cheap can you acquire.


Result as a service. Not lead. Not software.

Open invitation.


If you've cracked any part of the conversion system training, automation, experience, referrals, anything — drop a comment.

Tell me what you do and why it drives results.


One criteria only: Result as a service. Not lead. Not software.

Let's sell together.
author: Chitrak Shah

title: 4.5 Lakh Trees In 6 Years: A Different Story Of The Riverfront
descriptions:
Sabarmati Riverfront was once criticised as a “concrete project.”

But the numbers tell a different story.


In the last 6 years (2019–2025), the Riverfront has undergone a quiet ecological transformation:

• 4.5 lakh trees and shrubs planted

• 2.5 lakh+ trees and 1.65 lakh shrubs added across the stretch

• Miyawaki forests created using native species

• 35+ bird species now nesting in the biodiversity park

• Fruit-bearing trees like mango, jamun, orange and custard apple planted to support urban wildlife


What was once known mainly for promenades and urban design is slowly evolving into Ahmedabad’s largest urban biodiversity corridor.

The bigger shift is not aesthetic, it’s climatic.


More trees mean lower heat, better micro-climate, improved biodiversity and healthier urban spaces.

But this raises an important question for Ahmedabad:


If the Riverfront can plant 4.5 lakh trees in six years,


why can’t the rest of the city adopt the same scale of urban greening?


Urban development and ecology don’t have to compete.

The Riverfront is proving they can grow together.
author: Chitrak Shah

title: India Is Rising as a Global Destination for Real Estate Capital
descriptions:
India’s real estate sector is gaining stronger recognition in global investment markets. Recent industry data shows that the country has emerged as the fourth-largest global destination for land and development capital, reflecting increasing investor confidence in India’s long-term real estate growth.


This rise comes even as overall real estate investment activity across the Asia-Pacific region faced short-term moderation. Total investment across nine major APAC markets reached $71.9 billion in the first half of 2025, slightly lower than the previous year due to global economic uncertainty.


Despite these regional headwinds, India continues to stand out because of its expanding urban infrastructure, strong domestic capital participation, and consistent demand across residential and commercial real estate segments.


Key Insights

1. India is becoming a major destination for global capital

The country’s rise to fourth place globally highlights growing confidence among international investors in India’s property market.

2. Domestic investment is strengthening the sector

Domestic capital deployment in Indian real estate increased around 53% year-on-year, providing stability even during periods of global volatility.

3. Core real estate segments continue to attract investors

Residential and office developments together accounted for more than half of the investment activity during the period.


India’s growing prominence in global real estate rankings signals a broader shift in the investment landscape. As domestic capital deepens and international investors continue to explore emerging markets, India’s real estate sector is increasingly being viewed as a long-term global investment opportunity.
author: Chitrak Shah

title: Policy Changes Could Open New Global Funding Channels for Real Estate
descriptions:
Financing has always been one of the biggest challenges for large real estate and redevelopment projects in India. However, recent regulatory reforms could significantly change how developers access capital.


India has introduced changes to its External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) framework, allowing a wider range of companies to raise funds from overseas lenders and private credit funds. These reforms remove certain pricing caps on offshore loans and expand the types of projects that can receive international financing.


For the real estate sector, this could be particularly important. Historically, strict regulations limited the ability of developers to raise foreign debt. The revised framework now allows overseas borrowing to support construction and development projects, including township developments, commercial projects, and large urban infrastructure initiatives.


Industry experts believe these changes could unlock a new pool of global private credit, helping finance capital-intensive redevelopment projects that often struggle to secure domestic funding.


Key Insights

1. Access to global capital is expanding

The updated ECB rules allow more entities to raise overseas loans, broadening financing options for developers.

2. Private credit funds may enter the Indian market

Global lenders and investment funds could begin financing redevelopment and large-scale urban projects.

3. Competition in real estate financing may increase

The entry of international lenders could reshape the financing landscape traditionally dominated by domestic NBFCs and housing finance companies.


Access to capital often determines how quickly cities can redevelop and expand.

If global private credit begins flowing into India’s property sector, it could accelerate large-scale redevelopment, urban infrastructure, and commercial real estate development across the country.
author: Chitrak Shah

title: Overseas Market Uncertainty Could Strengthen India’s Housing Demand
descriptions:
Global economic uncertainty and rising geopolitical tensions are beginning to influence how wealthy Indians and NRIs approach property investments.


In recent years, many Indian investors diversified their portfolios by purchasing residential properties in global markets such as Dubai, London, and parts of Europe. However, growing instability in West Asia and economic uncertainty in the United States are prompting some investors to reassess overseas investments and consider redirecting capital toward India’s housing marketIndustry experts note that NRIs already play a significant role in India’s residential sector, contributing around 15–20% of overall housing demand, with a large share of this demand originating from the Gulf region.


With India continuing to receive strong remittance inflows and maintaining steady economic growth, the domestic housing market is increasingly viewed as a relatively stable investment destination for global Indians.


Key Insights

1. Global instability is reshaping investment preferences

Tensions in West Asia and economic uncertainty in major economies are encouraging investors to reconsider overseas property purchases.

2. NRI buyers remain a major demand driver

Non-resident Indians already account for a substantial share of residential property demand across several Indian cities.

3. Premium housing markets could see renewed interest

Cities such as Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Gurugram may benefit as investors explore domestic opportunities instead of international real estate.


Capital often gravitates toward stability during uncertain times.

If global volatility continues, India’s residential real estate market could see renewed participation from overseas investors seeking long-term security and growth.
author: Chitrak Shah

title: Rising Temperatures Are Making Sustainable Buildings More Important
descriptions:
Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar recently recorded temperatures above 40°C in early March, highlighting how extreme heat events are arriving earlier each year.


According to weather reports, Ahmedabad touched around 41.4°C about 7°C above the seasonal average, prompting heat alerts across several districts in Gujarat.


These rising temperatures are not only a climate concern they are also becoming an important factor in how cities design buildings and plan urban development.


As cities heat up, buildings that prioritize energy efficiency, natural ventilation, and green design are becoming increasingly relevant. Sustainable architecture can reduce indoor heat, lower energy consumption, and improve overall living comfort in dense urban environments.


Key Insights

1. Climate is becoming a design factor in real estate

Extreme heat is pushing developers to rethink building materials, ventilation systems, and urban planning strategies.

2. Green buildings help reduce energy demand

Sustainable construction can lower electricity usage by improving insulation, shading, and natural airflow.

3. Health and comfort are becoming central to housing design

Homes designed with sustainable principles can maintain better indoor temperatures and air quality.

 Shivalik Group have increasingly focused on environmentally conscious construction, incorporating sustainable architecture and green building practices across several projects.

These initiatives aim to create living environments that are more energy-efficient, environmentally responsible, and comfortable for residents.


As climate conditions evolve, sustainability in real estate is no longer just an environmental choice.

It is gradually becoming a practical necessity for building resilient and future-ready cities.
author: Chitrak Shah

title: Ahmedabad Metro Expansion Could Reshape the GIFT Corridor
descriptions:
Ahmedabad’s transport infrastructure is continuing to evolve. Recently, the Union Cabinet approved a ₹1,067-crore extension of the Ahmedabad Metro connecting GIFT City to Shahpur, creating a new 3.33-km elevated corridor with multiple stations.

The objective is clear: improve connectivity between Ahmedabad’s core city areas and the rapidly growing GIFT financial district.


Key Insights

1. Transit connectivity reduces travel friction

Direct metro access will make commuting between Ahmedabad and GIFT City significantly easier.

2. Transit corridors attract development

Historically, areas around metro lines often see new residential and commercial projects.

3. Institutional demand strengthens office markets

Better connectivity helps financial districts attract talent and global firms.


Transport infrastructure does more than move people.

It often determines where the next wave of real estate development will occur.

title: India’s Tier-2 Cities Are Emerging as Real Estate Growth Engines
descriptions:
For many years, India’s real estate activity was concentrated in major metropolitan cities. However, the growth pattern is gradually shifting as Tier-2 cities begin to attract stronger investment and development momentum.

Improved infrastructure, industrial expansion, and government initiatives such as PM Gati Shakti and regional economic corridors are strengthening connectivity and economic activity across emerging urban centres.


Cities like Ahmedabad, Indore, Surat, and Jaipur are increasingly becoming important contributors to India’s property market. In fact, Ahmedabad alone contributed around 8% of India’s residential sales value, generating nearly ₹67,000 crore in housing transactions, reflecting the growing importance of Tier-2 markets.


Key Insights

1. More affordable real estate

Property prices in Tier-2 cities remain significantly lower than metro markets, making homeownership and investment more accessible.

2. Infrastructure is improving connectivity

Expressways, industrial corridors, and logistics networks are strengthening regional economic activity.

3. Businesses are expanding beyond metros

Companies are increasingly setting up operations in emerging cities to reduce costs and access new talent pools.


Strategic Insight

India’s next phase of real estate growth may not be led by megacities alone.

It is likely to be shaped by rapidly developing Tier-2 urban centres that combine affordability, infrastructure growth, and expanding economic opportunities.

Ahmedabad’s strength lies in consistency, not speculation.

2. Shift toward larger homes

Improved connectivity, expanding ring roads, and economic growth corridors are steadily strengthening the city’s residential market.


Strategic Insight

Ahmedabad’s housing growth is not fueled by speculation.

It is being built on steady economic expansion, infrastructure development, and end-user demand - making it one of the most stable real estate markets in India today.

title: If you had ₹10 crore today — how would you invest it in Ahmedabad real estate?
descriptions:
Abhishek known as a number guy,

Asked me a question during a podcast.

If you are an HNI with 10 crore to invest in,

Ahmedabad real estate how will you split it?


Warehouses, high street, offices, land, houses?


I told him something simple.

Gujaratis never start with “where to invest.”

We start with “ketla chhutse.”

That means, how much will I really get back?


Second, you must ask:

Do you want regular rental income?

Or do you want only appreciation?

Based on that, here is how I would do it.


Office – 30%.

Because commercial rental gives steady income.


Retail – 30%.

It is risky, but if it works, the returns are the highest.


Warehousing – 30%.

Here you get both rental and land appreciation,

Because it is horizontal.


I skipped house and land.

Because in 10 crore,

I will not get the kind of land I want in the right place.

And if I had one more choice,

I would put money in a real estate fund.


That way I can invest across all categories,

Without managing each one myself.


Then Abhishek asked the question.

He asked, what if the amount was 100 crore instead of 10 crore?


My answer was different.

I would keep 10–15 crore for a good house.

Because local presence also matters.

Then 30–40% into commercials.

And the rest into funds or upcoming projects,

Purely for appreciation.


In real estate, it is not about asset class first.

It is about your purpose.

Rental income or appreciation.


So let me ask you.

If you had 10 crore today to invest in Ahmedabad,

how would you split it?

title: Shivalik Curv Sets Record for Gujarat’s Largest Single-Pour Raft Foundation
descriptions:
Engineering History: Shivalik Group Executes Gujarat’s Largest Single-Pour Rafting at Shivalik Curv


At Shivalik Group, we believe in not just building spaces but creating history. With immense pride, we announce a groundbreaking milestone that redefines engineering excellence in Gujarat’s real estate landscape. Our latest achievement? The successful completion of the state’s largest-ever single-pour raft foundation at our upcoming landmark project, Shivalik Curv.


Redefining the Limits of Engineering


Shivalik Curv isn’t just another high-rise. Designed to emulate the fluid, organic form of a seashell, the architectural brilliance of this structure demanded a foundation that matched its futuristic vision. Rising to the challenge, our engineering and project management teams came together to execute a single-pour rafting of 11,200 cubic meters of concrete at a depth of 5.4 meters — the first of its kind in Gujarat.

This continuous pour spanned 91 hours non-stop, a feat that required not only advanced machinery and skilled manpower but also extreme precision and planning. With this, Shivalik Curv surpasses our own previous benchmark set at Shivalik Skyview (8,800 cubic meters at 3 meters depth), raising the bar once again.


The Numbers Behind the Feat

  • Concrete Volume: 11,200 cubic meters
  • Raft Depth: 5.4 meters
  • Pour Duration: 91 hours (non-stop)
  • Steel Used: 2,500+ metric tonnes (16 layers of 40mm steel)
  • Steel Cost: ₹15 Crore
  • Concrete Cost: ₹7.5 Crore
  • Transit Mixers Used: 1,600
  • High-Performance Pumps: 8
  • Quality Engineers on Site: 8
  • Construction Workforce: 250+ skilled laborers for 85 days
  • Concrete Plants Active: 8 (each with dedicated QC engineers)
  • Transit Mixers Rejected for QC: 75-80


Quality at the Core


What sets this feat apart is not just its scale, but our uncompromising focus on quality. To maintain the required temperature during pouring, we used temperature-controlled concrete maintained between 26-27°C with ice infusion. For the first time in Gujarat, real-time concrete sensors were used to monitor temperatures continuously for 7-8 days post-pour.

More than 75 transit mixers were rejected on-site due to non-compliance with our strict QC standards — a reflection of our zero-tolerance policy towards quality deviation.


Precision. Discipline. Innovation.


Executing a raft of this scale meant running a tightly coordinated operation involving multiple stakeholders, real-time monitoring, logistical precision, and above all, disciplined teamwork. With partnerships like Hindustan and UltraTech for concrete supply, and the support of 250+ skilled workers and experts, the execution of Shivalik Curv’s foundation was nothing short of a construction symphony.


A Landmark for the Future


This engineering milestone is more than a record — it’s a symbol of what Shivalik Group stands for: innovation, excellence, and the relentless pursuit of redefining Gujarat’s skyline. Shivalik Curv is not just a project; it’s a landmark in the making at GIFT City, and this foundation is its heart.
